findings.issue_text: **`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44-47` — permission logic is wrong and unsafe.**
**`addGuests.handler.ts:52-56, 130-136` — the handler acts with the caller's credentials, not the booking owner's.**
**`addGuests.handler.ts:48` + no volume limit — unbounded email fan-out / data leak.**
**`addGuests.handler.ts:83-88` — case-sensitive comparisons defeat both the dedupe and the blacklist.**
**`addGuests.handler.ts:166-170` — failures are swallowed / partial-failure semantics undefined.**

**`apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:25-29`** — the zod schema is rebuilt on every render and duplicates the server schema; `.refine(...)` has no message, and the dedupe check is case-sensitive (client accepts `A@x.com`/`a@x.com`, server drops one). Hoist it to module scope and share the schema with `addGuests.schema.ts`.

**`AddGuestsDialog.tsx:39-42`** — `const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`` is always truthy, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is dead code and users see raw codes like `BAD_REQUEST: emails_must_be_unique_valid`.

**`packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:26`** — `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` will throw on an empty attendee list; other templates in this dir guard this. Also the new guest's name is `""`, so the subject may render "Guests Added: X with  at ...".

**`packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:11`** — reassigns the `value` prop (`value = value || []`); use a local const. `key={index}` on an editable list will misbehave when a middle row is removed (React reuses the input state). The `addOnSuffix` button has no `onClick` and relies on `onClickAddon` firing — fragile coupling worth a comment or restructure.

**`packages/ui/form/MultiEmailLazy.tsx:4`** — the comment "These are like 40kb" is copy-pasted from `PhoneInputLazy`; `MultiEmail` has no heavy dependency, so the dynamic import adds a round trip for no benefit.

**Locales** — only `en` strings were added (expected for this repo's Crowdin flow). `guests_added_event_type_subject` and `new_guests_added` are referenced from `packages/emails`, which resolves translations from the same bundle — verify at runtime.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44-47` — permission logic is wrong and unsafe.**

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. That requires the user to be BOTH a team admin and a team owner to pass, which contradicts the name/intended meaning (“admin OR owner”). This is a concrete logic bug in the permission check and will incorrectly deny access to legitimate users who are only one of the two (e.g., admin but not owner).

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`addGuests.handler.ts:52-56, 130-136` — the handler acts with the caller's credentials, not the booking owner's.**

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler explicitly builds the `EventManager` using the authenticated caller (`ctx.user`) and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. However, permission logic allows non-organizers (e.g., an attendee) to call this mutation (`isAttendee` branch). In those cases, the calendar update will run with the attendee’s credentials rather than the booking owner/organizer’s credentials, which is a concrete correctness/security issue: it can fail to update the organizer’s calendar event or attempt changes using the wrong account.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`addGuests.handler.ts:48` + no volume limit — unbounded email fan-out / data leak.**

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `addGuests` mutation whose input schema (`ZAddGuestsInputSchema`) allows an arbitrary-length `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` or other server-side cap. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler will `createMany` attendees for all `uniqueGuests` and then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which fans out email sending across organizer/team members and *every* attendee in `calendarEvent.attendees`. Since there is no bound on the number of guests a caller can submit, this enables unbounded outbound email fan-out (spam/DoS risk) and, because attendees are allowed to call this endpoint (permission check allows `isAttendee`), an attendee can invite arbitrary external emails and cause event details to be emailed to them (potential data leak by design/abuse).

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`addGuests.handler.ts:83-88` — case-sensitive comparisons defeat both the dedupe and the blacklist.**
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is that blacklist checking is effectively case-sensitive because only the blacklist entries are lowercased, not the input guest emails, allowing uppercase variants to bypass. The candidate explicitly flags case-sensitive comparisons defeating the blacklist (and also mentions dedupe), which matches the same underlying problem.

adjudication.rationale: The handler does not check any “state” fields (e.g., cancelled/confirmed/past, etc.) before allowing guest addition, but the diff also doesn’t show what booking-state fields exist or any requirement that adding guests must be blocked in certain states. As written, it validates existence and authorization, then updates attendees. Calling this a defect is speculative without a defined state model/constraints in the diff.

Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, after filtering input `guests` down to `uniqueGuests` (excluding already-attending and blacklisted emails) and only creating DB attendees for `uniqueGuests`, it calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (the original unfiltered list). In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (`email-manager.ts`), the `newGuests` list is used to decide which attendees are treated as “new” (`if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))`). Passing the unfiltered `guests` can incorrectly mark existing attendees (whose email was included in the request) as “new”, causing them to receive the wrong email template (Scheduled vs AddGuests). This is a verifiable logic bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`addGuests.handler.ts:166-170` — failures are swallowed / partial-failure semantics undefined.**

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts` the code wraps `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` in a `try/catch` and on error only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` (not even logging the actual error) and then continues to return `{ message: "Guests added" }`. This makes the mutation report success even when notifications fail, and the behavior/semantics for that partial failure are not defined or communicated to the caller.

The diff adds new UI, TRPC mutation, and email templates, but it does not add or modify any test files. However, "No tests whatsoever" is a generalized process critique rather than a concrete, verifiable defect (bug/security/correctness issue) introduced by the code itself. From the diff alone, we can only confirm tests weren’t added here, not that the change is incorrect or broken because of it.

The diff adds a new action item `{ id: "add_members", ... }` to the `actions` array in `BookingListItem.tsx` without any client-side conditional checks, so it is indeed “unconditional” in that sense. However, the diff does not establish that this is incorrect or a defect: other actions in the same array also appear unconditional, and the server-side `addGuests` mutation enforces permissions (FORBIDDEN if unauthorized). Without an explicit requirement or existing pattern in the diff showing it must be gated, this is a UX preference/speculation rather than a verifiable bug introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:25-29`** — the zod schema is rebuilt on every render and duplicates the server schema; `.refine(...)` has no message, and the dedupe check is case-sensitive (client accepts `A@x.com`/`a@x.com`, server drops one). Hoist it to module scope and share the schema with `addGuests.schema.ts`.

adjudication.rationale: AddGuestsDialog does define a Zod schema inside the component, so it is recreated on each render, but that is at most a minor performance/style concern and not a clear defect. The claim about duplicating the server schema is not verifiably a problem here (the server schema in addGuests.schema.ts does not include the client’s uniqueness refine, so they are intentionally different). The case-sensitivity mismatch described is also not supported by the diff: the server handler does not dedupe guest emails against each other at all, so it would not “drop one” of `A@x.com`/`a@x.com`—it would attempt to create both unless constrained elsewhere. The lack of a `.refine` message is not a correctness bug since the UI uses a separate `isInvalidEmail` flag/message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`AddGuestsDialog.tsx:39-42`** — `const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`` is always truthy, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is dead code and users see raw codes like `BAD_REQUEST: emails_must_be_unique_valid`.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the `onError` handler builds `message` using a template literal: ``const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;``. A template literal always produces a (non-empty) string, even when `err.data?.code` is `undefined` (e.g., it becomes "undefined: …"). Therefore `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` will never use the fallback, making it dead code. The toast will also always include the raw error code prefix (e.g., `BAD_REQUEST:`), which is visible to users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:26`** — `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` will throw on an empty attendee list; other templates in this dir guard this. Also the new guest's name is `""`, so the subject may render "Guests Added: X with  at ...".

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the subject interpolation uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` with no null/length guard. In the new add-guests flow, newly-created guests are persisted with `name: ""` (`addGuests.handler.ts` builds `guestsFullDetails` with empty name), and the email event attendees list is built from DB attendees without enforcing a non-empty name or deterministic ordering. This can lead to a subject like `Guests Added: ... with  at ...` if the first attendee has an empty name, and it also risks a runtime throw if `attendees` is ever empty when this template is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:11`** — reassigns the `value` prop (`value = value || []`); use a local const. `key={index}` on an editable list will misbehave when a middle row is removed (React reuses the input state). The `addOnSuffix` button has no `onClick` and relies on `onClickAddon` firing — fragile coupling worth a comment or restructure.

adjudication.rationale: The `key={index}` issue is a verifiable correctness problem in this diff: `MultiEmail` renders an editable, removable list (`value.map(... key={index})`), and removal uses `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)` which shifts indices/keys. React will reuse DOM nodes for subsequent rows, which can cause inputs to appear to “move” (cursor/focus/state) when deleting a middle row—this is the classic misbehavior of index keys in mutable lists. By contrast, `value = value || []` is just a local reassignment (not mutating the parent) and is mostly a style nit, and the "button has no onClick" point depends on `EmailField` internals (not shown), so it’s not strictly verifiable. Still, the index-key problem is real and present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`packages/ui/form/MultiEmailLazy.tsx:4`** — the comment "These are like 40kb" is copy-pasted from `PhoneInputLazy`; `MultiEmail` has no heavy dependency, so the dynamic import adds a round trip for no benefit.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `MultiEmailLazy.tsx` using `next/dynamic` with a comment claiming the component is “like 40kb”. However, nothing in the diff verifies MultiEmail’s bundle size or dependency weight, nor that the dynamic import is unjustified. This is a performance/style judgment (and possibly an inaccurate comment), not a clear, verifiable defect introduced by the change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new i18n keys only to `apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json` and then references those keys from the emails code via `this.t(...)` / `getTranslation(..., "common")`.
